rules.statement: State the purposes for which personal data is processed (processing includes collection, storage, use, provision, destruction and similar acts).
Each purpose is specific and clear; do not use open-ended wording such as "~등".
For consent-based processing, purposes match what was notified when consent was obtained.
For processing without consent, state purposes clearly enough that the data subject can reasonably expect them.
Where several services exist, purposes may be grouped per service.
Purposes may be merged with items (S03) and retention (S05) in one table, but then every element required by S03 and S05 must still be present.

goodPatterns: One numbered entry per task (e.g. member management, delivery of goods, service analysis, new-service development), each with a sentence listing concrete sub-purposes.
Lead-in states data is not used beyond these purposes and that a purpose change triggers separate consent or other required steps under PIPA Art. 18.
Integrated table columns: legal basis, purpose, items, retention.

commonDefects.defect: Purpose headings ending in "등" or bundling unrelated tasks (e.g. sign-up and service development etc.).
Purpose in policy differs from the purpose shown on the consent screen.
Marketing purpose hidden inside a general 'service provision' purpose.

extractionHints: consent-screen wording quoted by the speaker
watch for "등" and "서비스 개선" without detail

PIPA:3(1).at: provision text read in the law.go.kr XML (domain self-review)
